description: Calculate Publix Deli calories, protein, carbs and fat. Free Publix Deli nutrition calculator with complete menu data for all items.
articleHtml:
Publix Deli nutrition is different from a typical sandwich restaurant because there is rarely just one way to order an item.

A turkey Pub Sub can use Publix turkey or Boar’s Head OvenGold turkey. You can order a Half or Whole sub, change the bread, switch the cheese, add double meat, remove mayonnaise, add avocado, choose a different sauce, or turn some sandwiches into wraps.

Then the Deli extends well beyond subs into chicken tenders, fried chicken, prepared meals, sliced meats and cheeses, Grab & Go foods, salads, soups, family meals, and party platters.

Use the Publix Deli Nutrition Calculator above to match the exact product and customization you actually order.

Start With the Serving Format

For a Publix sub, identify:

Half or Whole

before calculating anything else.

Publix currently sells many of its made-to-order subs in both portions.

The serving size matters because the bread, meat, cheese, toppings, and condiments all scale with the order.

A Half Turkey Sub should therefore never inherit the nutrition of a Whole Turkey Sub.

A Pub Sub Is a Custom Meal, Not One Fixed Number

Publix's current online ordering system lets customers customize sandwiches with:

Bread

Cheese

Meat

Extra meat

Vegetables

Condiments

Sauces

and other additions.

This means a Pub Sub name is better treated as a starting recipe.

For example:

Turkey Sub + Provolone + lettuce + tomato

is not nutritionally identical to:

Turkey Sub + double meat + Swiss + mayonnaise + avocado + sub dressing .

The calculator should build the order from the selected configuration.

Bread Can Add Hundreds of Calories Before the Filling

Current Publix online product information lists whole-sub bread choices around:

White Sub Roll: approximately 470 calories

Whole Wheat Sub Roll: approximately 440 calories

Italian Five-Grain Sub Roll: approximately 540 calories.

Availability can vary by location.

The bread alone is therefore a substantial part of a Whole Pub Sub.

If you switch from one roll to another, NutritionSolver should adjust the bread component rather than keeping the original sandwich total unchanged.

Do Not Assume Wheat Is Always Available

Publix's current online ordering pages sometimes specifically note that wheat rolls are unavailable for the selected market.

This is important for the calculator.

The nutrition database can preserve the wheat option, but the page should not imply that every bread is available at every Publix store at all times.

Availability and nutrition are separate fields.

Publix Meat and Boar’s Head Meat Need Separate Records

Publix Deli sells its own sliced meats and Boar’s Head products.

Those should not be merged just because the meat type sounds similar.

For example:

Publix Oven Roasted Turkey

and:

Boar’s Head OvenGold Turkey

can have different serving nutrition and sodium.

The same distinction applies to ham, roast beef, and other deli meats.

A strong calculator should first ask:

Publix Deli or Boar’s Head?

and then apply the correct meat portion.

The Publix Turkey Sub Is Currently Around 650 Calories Before Heavy Customization

The current Publix online ordering page lists a standard Publix Deli Turkey Sub at approximately:

650 calories

with oven-roasted turkey, Provolone, lettuce, and tomato.

The sandwich can then be modified with different cheese, extra meat, bacon, avocado, sauces, vegetables, and condiments.

That makes the 650-calorie figure a useful standard starting configuration rather than a guarantee for every Turkey Sub.

Boar’s Head Turkey Has a Similar Starting Point but Different Ingredients

The current Boar’s Head Turkey Sub is also shown around:

650 calories

in a standard current configuration.

It uses Boar’s Head OvenGold Turkey Breast rather than the Publix-branded turkey.

Even when two finished sandwiches have similar headline calories, their underlying meat nutrition and sodium can differ.

Keep them as distinct menu entities.

The Ultimate Sub Should Be Built From Three Meats

Publix's current Ultimate Sub contains:

Tavern Ham

Oven Roasted Turkey Breast

Top Round Roast Beef

plus cheese, lettuce, tomato, bread, and selected condiments.

The current online ordering configuration is approximately:

680 calories

before optional customizations change the meal.

This should remain separate from Boar’s Head Ultimate because the meat products are not identical.

Italian Subs Need Publix vs Boar’s Head Distinction Too

Publix currently sells both Publix and Boar’s Head Italian-style subs.

The Publix Italian uses:

Genoa salami

Tavern ham

Cappy

Provolone

lettuce

tomato .

A current standard online configuration is approximately:

830 calories .

The Boar’s Head Italian uses its own branded meats and currently appears around:

800 calories in a standard online configuration.

Do not combine those two products under one generic Italian Sub .

Chicken Tender Sub Needs a Real Builder

The Chicken Tender Sub is one of Publix Deli's most recognizable sandwiches.

Publix currently describes it as hand-breaded chicken tenders with cheese, lettuce, tomato, and customer-selected fixings.

A current standard online configuration is shown at approximately:

1,040 calories .

But Publix's broader current Deli catalog gives a much wider range of approximately:

450 to 1,955 calories per sub

because size and customization can change the order dramatically.

That is why one fixed Chicken Tender Sub calorie value is not enough.

Chicken Tender Sub Should Start With the Tenders

A useful calculator flow is:

Half or Whole

then:

Chicken tenders

then:

Bread

then:

Cheese

then:

Toppings

then:

Sauce or condiment .

This is more accurate than starting with one 1,000-plus-calorie sandwich and trying to subtract modifications afterward.

Buffalo Chicken Tender Sub Is a Different Current Recipe

Publix currently sells a Buffalo Chicken Tender Sub made with:

Chicken tenders

Buffalo sauce

cheese

and selected vegetables.

The live online ordering system currently shows a standard configuration around:

1,200 calories .

Buffalo sauce is therefore part of the finished recipe and should not simply be treated as a plain Chicken Tender Sub with an identical total.

Sweet & Spicy Chicken Tender Sub Needs Its Own Record

The current Sweet & Spicy version uses:

Publix chicken tenders

sweet sriracha sauce

spicy three-pepper cheese

plus the selected toppings.

A current configuration is approximately:

1,220 calories .

This should be searchable by its exact product name rather than grouped under generic chicken tender subs.

Chicken Bacon Ranch Can Be Much Higher

The current Chicken Bacon Ranch Tender Sub combines:

Chicken tenders

bacon

Provolone

lettuce

tomato

Buttermilk Ranch .

The current online configuration is shown at approximately:

1,835 calories .

This demonstrates how sauces and added meats can alter a Pub Sub far more than a few vegetable toppings.

Publix Also Has Current Specialty Tender Subs

Current online Publix listings include additional chicken-tender preparations such as:

Hot Honey Chicken Tender Sub

Chicken Parmesan Tender Sub

Nashville Hot Chicken Tender Sub

along with Buffalo and Sweet & Spicy options.

These should have a dedicated:

Chicken Tender Subs

category.

Do not bury them among only nine generic Subs records.

Mayonnaise Can Change the Total More Than Several Vegetables Combined

Current Publix online customizers show approximately:

Mayonnaise: 220 calories for the displayed whole-sub portion

while vegetable additions such as tomato or onion contribute far less.

This makes condiments one of the most important customization steps.

A user removing mayo needs the calculator to remove the actual published serving, not an arbitrary generic tablespoon estimate.

Sub Dressing Is Another Large Addition

Current online customization data shows Boar’s Head Sub Dressing around:

200 calories

for the displayed whole-sub serving.

That means:

Sub without dressing

and:

Sub with full dressing portion

can differ significantly.

The calculator should also distinguish regular sub dressing from other deli sauces.

Ranch Can Be Even More Substantial

The current Chicken Tender Sub customizer shows Buttermilk Ranch around:

410 calories

for the displayed serving.

That means a creamy condiment can sometimes alter the meal more than changing the meat by a small amount.

Keep condiments visible in the nutrition total rather than hiding them under toppings .

Honey Mustard Needs Current Serving Context

Publix's current customizer shows Boar’s Head Honey Mustard around 45 calories for one displayed sandwich serving.

The exact amount can depend on the product and serving context.

NutritionSolver should therefore store:

ingredient + portion + source

instead of one universal Honey Mustard value with no serving label.

Cheese Choice Should Be Part of the Builder

Current online Publix sub options include cheeses such as:

Provolone

White American

Yellow American

Swiss

Cheddar

Muenster

Pepper Jack

and other store-dependent choices.

A current Whole sub cheese portion can be around 70 to 90 calories in the online customizer depending on the cheese.

If someone removes cheese or changes the variety, the nutrition total should change.

Double Meat Should Use the Actual Sandwich Protein

Publix lets customers add double meat to many subs.

The calorie addition depends on which meat is in the sandwich.

For example, adding more turkey is not the same as adding more salami or a mixed Ultimate meat portion.

The calculator should link:

Double Meat

to the selected sandwich protein rather than apply one universal extra meat value.

Vegetables Should Still Be Counted, but Their Effect Is Smaller

Publix currently offers toppings such as:

Lettuce

Tomato

Onions

Black olives

Green peppers

Banana peppers

Jalapeños

Pickles

Cucumbers

Spinach

and seasonings.

Most contribute relatively few calories compared with bread, cheese, mayonnaise, ranch, bacon, or chicken tenders.

They still belong in the builder, especially where sodium or other nutrient information is available.

Wraps Need Their Own Bread Replacement

Publix Deli also sells wraps.

Current options can include:

White Wrap

Whole Wheat Wrap

Spinach Wrap

Tomato Wrap

Gluten-Free White Wrap

and other products depending on location.

A wrap should replace the sub roll in the calculation.

Do not add a wrap on top of a normal sub bread serving.

Chicken Tender Wrap Is Not the Same as the Chicken Tender Sub

Publix's current Deli catalog separately lists a Chicken Tender Wrap , with a broad calorie range because of customization.

That means:

Chicken Tender Sub

and:

Chicken Tender Wrap

need different base records.

The protein may be similar, but the bread format changes the final meal.

Publix Deli Is Much More Than Pub Subs

The Deli currently includes categories such as:

Deli Subs

Deli Meats and Cheeses

Fried Chicken

Oven-Roasted Chicken

Prepared Meals

Wraps

Salads

Soups

Grab & Go Sandwiches

Party Platters

Drinks

and other ready-to-eat foods.

A useful Publix Deli calculator should reflect those actual departments rather than behaving only like a sandwich shop.

Chicken Tenders Need Piece Count or Serving Weight

NutritionSolver currently has a Chicken Tenders record near 940 calories.

That value is not useful without telling the customer:

how many tenders

or:

what serving weight

it represents.

Publix also sells tender meals in defined piece counts.

Every tender record should therefore include a count or weight.

Family Chicken Meals Need Shared-Meal Logic

Publix currently sells a Chicken Tenders Meal for Four with:

12 chicken tenders

two 16 oz sides

bread

sauce .

Publix lists the complete meal around:

3,480 to 6,760 calories

or roughly:

870 to 1,690 calories per serving

depending on the selected sides and accompaniments.

That is exactly the kind of product that needs a family-meal builder.

Do not show the entire package total as though it were one person's meal.

Fried Chicken Wings Need Piece Count

Publix Deli currently sells fried chicken wings in multiple quantities, including large party orders.

A current 50-piece plain breaded wing listing gives approximately:

180 calories per wing .

NutritionSolver should therefore calculate:

wing type + number eaten

rather than store an unexplained single Fried Chicken Wing result.

Prepared Meals Need Their Included Sides

A Publix fried chicken or tender meal can include:

chicken

sides

bread

sauce .

The meal nutrition therefore depends on the exact configuration.

This is similar to a restaurant combo, but the grocery Deli can also sell components individually.

Keep both:

complete prepared meal

and:

individual component

available without double-counting.

Sliced Deli Meat Should Use Weight-Based Serving Sizes

Publix sells sliced meat by weight.

A useful meat record should therefore state something like:

2 oz

or:

28g

rather than simply:

Tavern Ham

with no context.

This is particularly important for shoppers using sliced meat at home rather than inside a Pub Sub.

Sliced Cheese Needs the Same Serving Discipline

Cheese sold at the Deli counter can be ordered by weight, while cheese used on a sub uses a sandwich portion.

Those two serving contexts may not be identical.

NutritionSolver should distinguish:

Deli-counter serving

from:

Whole-sub cheese portion

instead of using one unlabeled Provolone value everywhere.

Grab & Go Foods Are Their Own Product Type

Publix also sells premade sandwiches and other Grab & Go Deli products.

For example, a packaged Cuban Sandwich has its own defined nutrition and does not necessarily match a made-to-order customizable Cuban-style sub.

Keep:

Made to Order

and:

Grab & Go

as separate product statuses.

Party Platters Need Per-Person or Per-Piece Values

Current Publix Sub Selections platters can contain many individual sandwiches.

A current Medium platter is approximately:

3,120 to 6,960 calories per platter

and serves around 18 people , with individual sub portions around 130 to 290 calories depending on selection.

For catering, the useful calculation is:

whole platter

or:

number of pieces eaten .

A catering platter should never distort normal individual-meal statistics.

Publix Deli Nutrition Questions

How many calories are in a Publix Chicken Tender Sub?+
How many calories are in a Publix Turkey Sub?+
How many calories are in a Publix Ultimate Sub?+
How many calories are in a Publix Italian Sub?+
How many calories are in a Publix sub roll?+
How many calories does mayonnaise add to a Pub Sub?+
Does Publix have Boar’s Head subs?+
Where does Publix publish Deli nutrition?+

Build a Publix Deli Order From the Counter Forward

For a Pub Sub , choose:

Publix or Boar’s Head → Half or Whole → Bread → Meat → Cheese → Toppings → Condiments → Extras .

For chicken , choose the exact item and piece count, then add the selected sides, bread, and sauce.

For Grab & Go , use the packaged product's own serving information.

For family meals and platters , calculate either the entire package or the portion actually eaten.

Publix Deli has enough customization that one static calorie value is rarely the best answer. Matching the exact counter order produces a much more useful nutrition total.
